# Pop-out hover-sync e2e judges a scroll inside its warm-up's burst

## Context

`e2e-brain` goes red on `WorkstationPopOutHoverSyncNL.spec.mjs:90`, on both attempts, always in one shape:

```
Expected: ArrayContaining ["suspendHover", "resumeHover"]
Received: ["resumeHover"]
```

Seen on a docs-only `dev` push (`485c125712`, run 39079895583), an unrelated dependabot PR (run 39216772503) and `#19871` (run 39303646187, shard 9/10). Locally at `21053bd97b`: 1 red in 10 (`--repeat-each=10 --retries=0`, own Bridge on `NEO_NL_PORT=8191`).

## The Problem

The witness counts `suspendHover` / `resumeHover` at each window's `GridRowHoverSync` addon around one judged wheel scroll in the popup. Its judged scroll has never sent a suspend of its own.

An instrumented run (popup scroll events, `neo-is-scrolling` toggles, addon calls and wheel marks on one clock) shows why:

- When the popup loads, a scroll burst is usually open already, from the mount. That burst imports the addon, so the "addon exists" poll (`:142-143`) returns before the warm-up's scroll has even landed. The warm-up's scroll event arrives ~40 ms after its wheel, after the counters went on.
- The judged wheel (`:154`) fires ~25 ms after the warm-up wheel, inside that open burst. `ScrollManager` resumes only 150 ms after a burst's last scroll event, so the first call the counters see is that burst's `resumeHover`.
- The suspend that turned runs green came from somewhere else. The Workstation Feed appends a batch every 500 ms, and `grid.Body#onStoreLoad` scrolls a mounted grid to the top 50 ms after every store mutation, through `DomAccess.scrollTo`. The first tick after the burst ends opens a new one, and its suspend is the one the old assertion matched. When no burst was open at load, the warm-up's own suspend, landing after the counters, did the same job.
- A red is a tick whose `scrollTo(0)` lands inside the still-open burst. The grid then sits at the top, so every later tick's `scrollTo(0)` changes nothing and no suspend ever comes.

Measured on the old spec: with the Feed stopped it fails 4 of 5 runs. With the Feed stopped and 50 ms before the counters, so the warm-up's suspend lands first, it fails 5 of 5 with the CI shape.

## The Architectural Reality

Design authority: `GridRowHoverSync#suspendHover` is "invoked when a scroll interaction starts", and `#resumeHover` is called "when a scroll operation finalizes" (`src/main/addon/GridRowHoverSync.mjs:143,175`). The product does exactly this; the spec assumes one wheel is one interaction, and that nothing else scrolls the grid.

- `grid.ScrollManager#onContainerScroll` suspends only when `body.isScrolling` was false (`src/grid/ScrollManager.mjs:201`). `onScrollEnd`, a trailing 150 ms `buffer` (`:14`), clears the flag and resumes.
- `Workstation.store.Feed` produces every `intervalMs` (500), and `start()` runs on Workspace construction (`apps/workstation/view/Workspace.mjs:295`). Its public `stop()` pauses production without discarding records.
- The worker's grid `Body` holds `isScrolling` and the `scrollTop` that `grid.View#syncBodies` writes into it. The body's DOM id is its component id.
- `worker.App#getAddon` returns the cached proxy once a window has the addon (`src/worker/App.mjs:354`). So a finished burst has already posted its resume by the time a later Neural Link read can return.

## The Fix

Only `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationPopOutHoverSyncNL.spec.mjs` changes:

- Stop the Feed's producer through the Neural Link (`findInstances` + `callMethod(id, 'stop')`), as `WorkstationGridRepaintNL` already resolves the store.
- After the popup warm-up and before the counters, poll the window's scroll and the grid body (`app.getComponent(bodyId, ['isScrolling', 'scrollTop'])`) until the scroll has moved past its pre-warm-up value, the body has caught up with it, and the burst is closed.
- Assert exactly `['suspendHover', 'resumeHover']` in the popup. The judged scroll is now the only burst source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The judged wheel fires only after the worker reports the earlier burst over; the failure message shows the state it read.
- [ ] Red-first: the old spec with the Feed stopped and 50 ms before the counters fails every run; the fixed spec passes every run under the same delay.
- [ ] The fixed spec passes locally under `--repeat-each=20 --retries=0`.
- [ ] Control: with `ScrollManager` sending no `windowId` (the `#18295` regression), the fixed spec fails. It fails at the warning check, and at the count once that check is skipped.
- [ ] Hosted `e2e-brain` is green on the PR.

## Out of Scope

- `ScrollManager`'s burst semantics, which match the addon's JSDoc.
- Whether a ticking feed should scroll a grid the user scrolled back to the top every 500 ms. That is a product question, captured as a defect-note rather than a fix here.
- The opener side. Its warm-up ends more than 1 s before its counter goes on, and a stray opener call can only fail that assertion, never pass it.
- The other open `e2e-brain` intermittents, which belong to `#19655`'s quarantine set.

## Avoided Traps

- A fixed sleep before the judged wheel: it is still a race when the CPU is starved, and a running Feed would still add bursts.
- Reading `neo-is-scrolling` from the DOM: a poll can run before the class is added and call the burst over.
- Keeping `arrayContaining`: any burst at all satisfies it, which is how a tick passed for the judged scroll.
